Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 24-Dec-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE MAKEUP EXAMINATIONS - DECEMBER 2025  
  MACHINE LEARNING [CSE_4032]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                Apply the traditional K-Means clustering (partitional) algorithm with Euclidean distance to the       (5)  
  following 2D dataset:  
  A)  
  
  
  $$With k=2, use P2 and P5 as the initial cluster centers.$$  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           Analyze the major differences between agglomerative and divisive hierarchical clustering with         (5)  
  respect to:  
  
  Initial step and stopping condition,  
  Computational complexity, and Interpretability of the dendrogram.  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
2)                You are given data collected from a smart greenhouse monitoring system.                               (5)  
  The goal is to predict the plant health status (Healthy / Diseased) based on environmental and leaf  
  A)           condition features.  
  
  
  Apply the ID3 decision-tree algorithm with Entropy and Information Gain to construct a univariate  
  tree (depth = 1) that predicts the Status of each plant.  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)   Examine the relationship between pre-pruning, the bias-variance trade-off, and the resulting             (3)  
  generalization performance of decision tree models.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  C)   Describe the reason that causes the overall entropy after a dataset split to remain greater than zero (2)  
  when one child node is perfectly pure (entropy = 0.0) and the other has entropy 0.97, both being of  
  equal size.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3)        Examine the role of posterior cluster probabilities in quantifying ambiguity in data point assignments (4)  
  and analyze the limitations of deterministic methods such as K-Means in representing uncertainty  
  A)   within overlapping or noisy datasets.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)   Explain how Occam's Razor, the Ugly Duckling Theorem, and the No Free Lunch Theorem together (3)  
  highlight the challenges in building generalizable machine learning models. Support your answer  
  with one example scenario where these principles come into conflict.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  C)   A random forest model shows higher test accuracy than a single decision tree. Analyze what               (3)  
  property of bagging contributes to this improvement.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO6" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
4)        Differentiate the mathematical structure of the splitting criterion employed in a univariate decision    (4)  
  tree from that of a multivariate decision tree. Determine how the reliance on a single feature axis in  
  A)   the univariate approach enforces axis-aligned splits.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)                                                                                                            (3)  
  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  C)   Analyze how the choice of combination rule (majority, weighted, or median voting) impacts                (3)  
  ensemble robustness against noisy base-learners.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO6" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                                                                                                                 (5)  
  
  A)  
  
  
  Page #2

Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               Differentiate the roles of the ε--insensitive zone and the regularization parameter C in Support       (5)  
  Vector Regression (SVR). Determine how increasing the value of C structurally affects the  
  tolerance for training errors and the resulting width of the margin. Finally, analyze the precise  
  mechanism by which a higher C value shifts the model's behaviour towards reduced bias but  
  concurrently increases its variance and sensitivity to outlying data points.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"
